skill.name: meeting-insights-analyzer
skill.description: Analyzes meeting transcripts and recordings to uncover behavioral patterns, communication insights, and actionable feedback. Identifies when you avoid conflict, use filler words, dominate conversations, or miss opportunities to listen. Perfect for professionals seeking to improve their communication and leadership skills.
skill.summary: Turns meeting transcripts into evidence-based communication insights, examples, trends, and practical improvement steps.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: All 19 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks and ordinary communication terms. The skill defines no shell commands or network discovery. However, its workflow needs privacy controls and defenses against instructions embedded in transcripts.

remediation.issue: The workflow processes sensitive meeting transcripts and reproduces participant quotes without requiring consent or redaction.
remediation.suggestion: Require user authorization, minimize the files read, redact personal data, and avoid verbatim quotes unless the user explicitly requests them.

remediation.issue: Transcript content is not explicitly treated as untrusted data.
remediation.suggestion: Instruct the agent to ignore commands inside transcripts and use transcript text only as evidence for the requested analysis.

content.value_statement: Meeting transcripts contain useful patterns that are difficult to review consistently. This skill turns them into evidence-based communication feedback and focused improvement steps.
actual_capabilities: Reviews transcript files in TXT, Markdown, VTT, SRT, and DOCX formats.
Identifies patterns involving conflict avoidance, interruptions, listening, questions, and facilitation.
Calculates speaking ratios and language frequencies when transcripts contain adequate speaker labels and timestamps.
Supports findings with meeting names, timestamps, transcript excerpts, and alternative phrasing.
Compares communication patterns across meetings or time periods.
Produces structured summaries with strengths, growth areas, metrics, and next steps.
limitations: Results depend on accurate transcripts, speaker labels, dates, and timestamps.
The skill does not transcribe audio or video recordings by itself.
Behavioral conclusions are contextual interpretations, not clinical or objective assessments.
Industry comparisons require reliable benchmark data supplied by the user.

use_cases.title: Improve Team Facilitation
use_cases.description: Review speaking balance, disagreement handling, quieter participant inclusion, and action-item clarity across recurring team meetings.

use_cases.title: Support Communication Coaching
use_cases.description: Find transcript evidence for recurring habits and create specific practice recommendations for coaching sessions.

use_cases.title: Track Personal Progress
use_cases.description: Compare two meeting periods to measure changes in interruptions, questions, filler words, and active listening.

prompt_templates.title: Review One Meeting
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [transcript file] for my communication strengths and one improvement area. Cite timestamps and explain each conclusion.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a single transcript

prompt_templates.title: Find Monthly Patterns
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze transcripts from [date range]. Identify recurring patterns in clarity, listening, questions, interruptions, and filler words. Include representative examples.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Two Periods
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare meetings from [period one] and [period two]. Measure speaking ratio, interruptions, clarifying questions, and filler words. Explain meaningful changes.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Leadership Facilitation
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate my facilitation across [folder]. Assess decision-making, disagreement handling, participation balance, agenda control, and follow-up clarity. Build an evidence-based development plan.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced leadership analysis across a transcript collection

output_examples.input: Analyze this team meeting for active listening.
output_examples.output: The report identifies three clarifying questions and two paraphrases with timestamps. It also notes one missed response and recommends a specific follow-up phrase.

output_examples.input: Compare my meetings from the first and second quarters.
output_examples.output: The comparison shows fewer interruptions, more clarifying questions, and a stable speaking ratio. Each trend includes examples and a focused next step.

output_examples.input: Where did I avoid direct feedback?
output_examples.output: The analysis highlights hedging and indirect requests in several moments. It explains the likely impact and suggests clearer alternative wording for each example.

best_practices: Use consistent filenames and preserve speaker labels, dates, and timestamps.
Analyze one defined behavior before requesting a broad communication review.
Redact sensitive details and confirm participant consent before processing transcripts.
anti_patterns: Do not treat inferred motives or emotions as established facts.
Do not compare metrics across periods with different transcript quality or meeting types.
Do not share verbatim participant quotes without authorization.

faq.question: Which transcript formats can the skill review?
faq.answer: The instructions cover TXT, Markdown, VTT, SRT, and DOCX files. Readability depends on the selected tool and file structure.

faq.question: Can it analyze a recording without a transcript?
faq.answer: No. Obtain a transcript from the meeting platform or transcription service before analysis.

faq.question: How are speaking ratios calculated?
faq.answer: The skill uses speaker labels and timestamps to estimate each participant's speaking share. Missing metadata reduces accuracy.

faq.question: Can it compare communication changes over time?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide clearly separated date ranges and comparable meetings for more reliable trend analysis.

faq.question: Are the behavioral findings objective?
faq.answer: No. They are evidence-based interpretations that should be reviewed against meeting context and participant perspectives.

faq.question: How should sensitive transcripts be handled?
faq.answer: Use authorized files, redact unnecessary personal data, limit access, and avoid sharing verbatim quotes without consent.
